name: Sperm retention / abstinence rituals

lead: Semen retention means deliberately avoiding ejaculation, often with NoFap-style abstinence from masturbation and porn. People hope for more energy, focus, confidence and an attractive presence, and some expect higher testosterone.

Versions appear in Taoist texts and nineteenth-century karezza, and the modern online form grew from the NoFap community founded in 2011. The testosterone claim traces to a 2003 abstinence study that was retracted in 2021, and no trials test the appearance claims.

paras: Practitioners abstain for weeks or months, often tracking streaks in online communities and pairing it with exercise and other routines. Benefits are reported through personal accounts rather than measured outcomes.

Researchers have reported Dhat-like anxiety and relapse distress in men who follow retention groups, and analyses of social media content find retention material widely viewed and often inaccurate. Retention is not reliable contraception.

angle.text: Forum users practice semen retention or NoFap hoping for more energy, focus, confidence and attractiveness, and some expect higher testosterone. The headline testosterone study was retracted in 2021, so reported benefits come from personal accounts.

lead: Semen retention is the deliberate avoidance of ejaculation, for days, weeks or months, usually in the hope of channelling energy into work, training and social presence. It is often paired with NoFap-style abstinence from masturbation and pornography, and in looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a route to more drive, steadier mood, better gym output and a more confident, attractive presentation [1][2][3].

The idea has deep roots. Chinese cultivation texts, Hindu and yogic traditions of brahmacharya, the nineteenth-century Oneida Community's 'male continence' and Alice Stockham's 'karezza' all treated conserved semen as a store of vitality [4][5][6][7]. The modern online movement grew from the NoFap community founded in June 2011 after a Reddit thread about a 2003 abstinence-and-testosterone study, which was retracted in 2021 [3].

Published research on the practice itself is sparse. Urology researchers have analysed how semen-retention content performs on TikTok and Instagram, and have described a Dhat-like semen-loss anxiety in men drawn from retention and NoFap groups [8][9][10]. Clinicians quoted in coverage of NoFap say many claimed benefits lack medical support [3].

paras: Practitioners differ in how strict they are. Some avoid partnered sex and masturbation entirely; others practise coitus reservatus (intercourse without ejaculation) or allow occasional release on a schedule, as one looksmax.org poster describes saving it for weekends [1][4]. The NoFap community says its stated aim is supporting sexual health goals rather than necessarily lifelong abstinence, and many members count days in 'streaks' [3].

Participants commonly pair retention with lifting, cold exposure, meditation and cutting out pornography, so reported changes are hard to attribute to any single habit. In looksmaxxing spaces the appeal is usually stated in terms of energy for training, calmer emotional control, and a perceived boost in presence and eye contact [1].

In traditional Chinese medicine, jing ('essence') is one of the Three Treasures and is said to be consumed by stress, exertion, illness and sexual intemperance; practices that conserve it are central to longevity theories [6]. Taoist texts included methods summarised as retaining semen to replenish the brain [4].

In Hindu thought, brahmacharya is student-stage celibacy and later a wider discipline. Texts such as the Shandilya Upanishad and the Manusmriti call for abstaining from release of semen, and Patanjali's Yoga Sutra 2.38 says brahmacharya yields virya, read variously as strength, capacity or virility [5].

John Humphrey Noyes's Oneida Community, founded in 1848 in New York, practised 'male continence', in which men avoided ejaculation in sex; Noyes believed ejaculation drained men's vitality and published Male Continence in 1872 [7]. Alice Stockham coined 'karezza' in her 1903 book Karezza: Ethics of Marriage [4]. Sex reformers of the era were prosecuted under obscenity laws associated with Anthony Comstock [4].

Alexander Rhodes, a Pittsburgh web developer, founded NoFap in June 2011 after reading a Reddit thread about a 2003 study reporting that testosterone rose about 145.7 percent after seven days without masturbation; the subreddit launched on 20 June 2011 and Rhodes later built the standalone NoFap.com forum [3]. The 2003 paper was retracted in 2021 because it overlapped with another published article [3].

Anti-pornography advocate Gary Wilson's work is influential in the community, though critics note he lacks formal scientific credentials [3]. By August 2025 NoFap listed roughly 1.2 million users, and about 350,000 registered forum members as of January 2024 [3]. A 2014 survey found members overwhelmingly male [3].

Semen retention spread from NoFap and looksmax.org threads to short-video platforms, where men's-health hashtags are widely viewed [8]. On looksmaxxing forums the practice is a recurring topic, with posters describing more motivation and emotional control after a couple of days, and others arguing the effect is a placebo or that regular ejaculation supports testosterone [1][2].

Researchers and journalists have noted overlap between NoFap communities and the wider 'manosphere', including men's-rights and pickup-artist spaces, and some forum posts with conspiratorial content [3]. NoFap's leadership has also pursued legal action against critics and scientists, including a suit filed in 2026 against Aylo, UCLA, Taylor and Francis and researchers Nicole Prause and David Ley [3].

Proponents describe more energy, focus, ambition, social confidence, deeper voice, clearer skin and a more 'magnetic' presence. A looksmax.org poster reports feeling 'way more powerful' after about two days and plans to channel it into work; another says it is helpful for emotional control and motivation [1]. Another thread argues the reverse, that without regular sex the body adjusts testosterone downward, and that benefits are overstated [2].

A study searching TikTok and Instagram for terms including testosterone, erectile dysfunction, semen retention and vasectomy found men's-health content widely viewed and frequently inaccurate [8]. A later Wikipedia-summarised comparison reports that semen-retention and NoFap claims ranked among the least accurate [4]. A 2025 andrology review discusses social-media men's-health claims as separating science from speculation [10], and a 2024 paper reported that online ejaculation-training programs promote treatments not backed by evidence [11].

Physicians and psychologists quoted in coverage say many NoFap claims lack scientific support, and some researchers argue prolonged abstinence may harm mental health [3]. The DSM-5-TR and ICD-11 do not recognise pornography or sex addiction as diagnoses [3]. Coitus reservatus is not considered a reliable contraceptive or infection safeguard, because pre-ejaculate can carry sperm from an earlier ejaculation and infectious agents [4].

Dhat syndrome is a culture-bound condition, described mainly in South Asia, in which men worry that semen is being lost, with fatigue, anxiety, low mood and concerns about sexual performance; the term was coined by psychiatrist N. N. Wig in 1960 and cognitive behavioral therapy is described as the mainstay of treatment [12]. A study of 47 White British men found evidence of a similar semen-loss concern outside South Asia [13]. A 2024 paper reported Dhat syndrome emerging in the United States among men from anti-masturbation retention and NoFap groups [9].

No controlled trials of semen retention for appearance, training or confidence outcomes were found. The literature consists of content analyses of social media [8][10], reports of Dhat-type syndrome in Western men [9][13], and a review of online ejaculation-training programs [11]. The 2003 testosterone-after-abstinence paper that inspired the movement was retracted in 2021 [3].
Related practices include NoFap and pornography abstinence, karezza and coitus reservatus, brahmacharya, and Taoist jing-conservation exercises [4][3][5][6].
